pan-threshold.$description: Pointer travel that turns a press into a pan (below it, a press is a click).

pan-step.$description: Pan distance of one arrow key press (screen px).

fit-padding.$description: Space kept around the scene when it is fitted to the viewport (screen px).

badge.$description: Badge: a count or a dot on an icon, avatar or tab item that says new items are waiting. A count above max reads max+ (99+); a dot says only that something is new. The badge is decoration: the host carries the count in its accessible name ('Inbox, 3 unread'), so the badge itself is hidden from assistive technology.

min-size.$description: Count badge height and minimum width: one digit sits in a circle, more digits stretch it into a pill.

padding-inline.$description: Side padding of a count of two or more digits.

offset.$description: The badge's top and inline-end edges sit this far outside the host's top inline-end corner.

ring-width.$description: Ring around the badge in the ground behind the host, so the badge reads where it overlaps the icon.

ring.$description: Ring colour: the ground behind the host (a badge on another surface takes that surface's colour).

max-count.$description: Largest count shown; above it the badge reads max-count+ (99+).

background.$description: Accent badge ground. New items (the default tone).

foreground.$description: Badge: accent badge count.

background.$description: Danger badge ground. Items that need action: failures, overdue work.

foreground.$description: Badge: danger badge count.

background.$description: Neutral badge ground. Counts that inform without asking for attention.

foreground.$description: Badge: neutral badge count.

enter.$description: A badge appearing: it scales up from enter-scale and fades in. A changed count swaps without motion.

enter-scale.$description: Start scale of a badge appearing.

skeleton.$description: Skeleton: placeholders in the shape of content that is loading (text lines, a media block, an avatar). It appears only after delay, so a fast load never flashes it, and once shown it stays at least min-visible. It pulses gently and holds still under reduced motion. The loading region carries aria-busy and a status line for assistive technology; the placeholders are hidden from it.

bg.$description: Placeholder ground: the ink at 10% (12% in dark mode), so it reads on the canvas, on cards and on raised surfaces.

line-height.$description: Height of a text line placeholder.

last-line.$description: Width of the last line of a paragraph placeholder (% of the line).

delay.$description: Wait before a skeleton appears: a load that finishes sooner shows no placeholder (a timing rule, kept under reduced motion).

min-visible.$description: Once shown, a skeleton stays at least this long, so content does not flicker in after it.

empty-state.$description: Empty and error states: what a screen or region shows when it has nothing to list (empty), when a search or filter finds nothing (no-results), when loading failed (error) and when the device is offline (offline). An icon in a tile, a title that says what happened, one or two sentences that say what to do, and at most two actions, the first primary (error: Try again; no-results: Clear filters). An error state keeps the region's place in the layout; when it replaces content after the reader's own action, focus moves to its title.

padding-block.$description: Space above and below the state in its region.

gap.$description: Gap between the tile, the title and the body.

actions-gap.$description: Space between the body and the actions.

max-width.$description: Width of the text column (about 40 characters of body text).

icon.$description: Empty state: icon size.

title-type.$description: Empty state: title in a region.

title-type-page.$description: Title when the state fills a screen or a page (404, 500).

tile-bg.$description: Icon tile ground: Nothing here yet (inbox icon).

icon.$description: Icon: Nothing here yet (inbox icon).

tile-bg.$description: Icon tile ground: A search or filter found nothing (search-x icon).

icon.$description: Icon: A search or filter found nothing (search-x icon).

tile-bg.$description: Icon tile ground: Loading failed (circle-alert icon).

icon.$description: Icon: Loading failed (circle-alert icon).

tile-bg.$description: Icon tile ground: No connection (wifi-off icon).

icon.$description: Icon: No connection (wifi-off icon).

illustration-width.$description: Width of an illustration that replaces the icon tile in a page-size state (16:10, drawn to the illustration rules).

swipe-actions.$description: Swipe actions: a list row slides sideways to uncover up to three actions at its inline end (inline start for a second set). Released past open-ratio of the actions' width, or flung faster than interaction.gesture.fling-velocity, the row stays open; dragged past commit-ratio of the row's width it runs its first action (a full swipe) and the haptic role fires as the row crosses that line. Every action is also in the row's menu (a More button or a long press), which is the way in for keyboards, switches and screen readers. Destructive actions ask for no confirmation only when an Undo toast follows.

action-width.$description: Swipe actions: width of one action.

icon.$description: Swipe actions: action icon.

gap.$description: Gap between an action's icon and its label.

open-ratio.$description: A row released past this share of its actions' width stays open; short of it, it closes.

commit-ratio.$description: A row dragged past this share of its own width runs its first action (a full swipe).

settle.$description: The row settling closed, open at its actions, or out of the list after a full swipe.

background.$description: Destructive action ground: Delete, remove (trash-2 icon).

foreground.$description: Destructive action icon and label.

background.$description: Neutral action ground: Archive, mark as read, more (archive icon).

foreground.$description: Neutral action icon and label.

background.$description: Accent action ground: Pin, flag, the item's main quick action (pin icon).

foreground.$description: Accent action icon and label.

pull-refresh.$description: Pull to refresh: at the top of a scrolled list, pulling down past threshold arms a refresh and releasing starts it. The indicator follows the finger (at resistance of its travel, rubber-banded past max), turns to face down when armed, then spins while the refresh runs and stays at least min-visible. A status line announces Refreshing and Updated to assistive technology, and a Refresh button in the app bar or menu does the same job without the gesture.

threshold.$description: Pull distance (after resistance) that arms a refresh.

max.$description: Largest pull; past it the indicator rubber-bands (interaction.gesture.rubber-band).

resistance.$description: The indicator and the content move this share of the finger's travel.

rest.$description: Where the indicator holds while the refresh runs (its distance below the top edge of the list).

idle.$description: Indicator while pulling, before the threshold.

armed.$description: Indicator once armed and while refreshing.

settle.$description: The indicator settling back after a short pull, or to rest when a refresh starts.

min-visible.$description: A refresh holds its indicator at least this long, so a fast reload still reads as done.

launch-screen.$description: Launch screen: what shows between a tap on the app icon and the first frame: the canvas in the device's mode. iOS shows the ground alone, as the iOS guidelines ask (no logo, words, progress or animation), so the first screen replaces it without a jump (UILaunchScreen: build/ios/LaunchScreen.plist and the DPLaunchBackground colour set). Android 12 and later always draw the app icon on it (the SplashScreen API: build/android/res/values/dp_splash.xml). Installed web apps get the manifest's background colour, icon and name.

bg.$description: Launch ground, in the device's light or dark mode.

icon-bg.$description: Android: the disc behind the app icon (windowSplashScreenIconBackgroundColor), the icon's own ground.

exit.$description: Android: the hand-off to the first screen, a fade (SplashScreen.setOnExitAnimationListener); iOS fades by itself and the web shows no launch screen of its own.

avatar.$description: Avatar: a person or an account as a photo, their initials or a person icon in a circle, at four sizes. Initials sit on a fill theme (sage unless the host names another with .dp-fill-<name>), so a list of people reads as a set of colours without any one of them meaning something. A group overlaps its avatars, rings each in the ground colour and ends with a +N count past group-max. Next to a visible name the avatar is decoration and hidden from assistive technology; alone, it carries the person's name as its label.

diameter.$description: SM avatar diameter. Dense lists, bylines in tables, group stacks in a row.

icon.$description: Person icon in a SM avatar.

diameter.$description: MD avatar diameter. List rows and comments.

group-max.$description: Avatars shown in a group before the +N count.

overflow-background.$description: Ground of the +N count at the end of a group.

stepper.$description: Stepper: a number chosen in steps with a minus and a plus button around the value (quantities, guests, minutes). Each button stops at its limit, turns disabled there and plays the limit haptic when pressed at the limit; holding a button repeats the step after repeat-delay every repeat-interval. On the web the value is an input the reader can also type into and change with the arrow keys; assistive technology reads it as a spin button with its value, minimum and maximum.

value-min-width.$description: Minimum width of the value between the buttons (three tabular digits).

icon.$description: Stepper: minus and plus icons.

button-radius.$description: Hover and pressed grounds inside the group.

border.$description: Group border (3:1 against the canvas, like a field).

border-disabled.$description: Group border when the whole stepper is disabled.

value-disabled.$description: Value when the stepper is disabled.

focus-ring.$description: Focus ring on the focused button or the value.

repeat-delay.$description: Holding a button repeats the step after this delay (a timing rule, kept under reduced motion).

repeat-interval.$description: Interval between repeated steps while a button is held (a timing rule, kept under reduced motion).

page-dots.$description: Page dots: where the reader is in a short run of pages (onboarding, a carousel): one dot per page, the current one stretched into a pill in ink. The dots show position; they are not the way to move, which is the carousel's swipe, its previous and next buttons and the arrow keys. Assistive technology reads the position as text ('Page 2 of 5').

carousel.$description: Carousel: a horizontal run of slides that snaps one slide at a time (onboarding, media, featured cards). A swipe or a scroll moves it; the previous and next buttons and the arrow keys move it without a gesture; page dots show where the reader is. It never moves on its own. The next slide peeks in at the inline end so the run reads as more than one; slides out of view are inert, and the new position is announced politely.

controls-gap.$description: Gap between the page dots and the previous and next buttons.

progress-steps.$description: Progress steps: where the reader is in a flow of three to five steps (sign-up, checkout, setup). Each step has a marker and a short label: done steps show a check, the current step is outlined in ink with its number, and upcoming steps are muted. Past five steps, or where the labels do not fit, the compact form says 'Step 2 of 5' over a bar. The list is ordered, the current step carries aria-current='step' and done steps say so in words.

Picking an option closes the sheet, plays the change haptic and returns focus to the trigger. Past search-from options the sheet starts with a search field. On the web the options are a radio group, so the arrow keys move between them.

tooltip.$description: Tooltip: the name of a control whose name is not visible (an icon button), shown on hover and on keyboard focus after delay, and on a long press on touch, where it stays for dwell after the finger lifts; Escape, blur and pointer leave hide it. It names; it never holds actions or anything the reader needs to go on, and it never covers the control it names. One at a time.

It sits on a fill theme (sage unless the host names another); the control it points at keeps working and gets a spotlight ring. Escape and Done close it for good. One at a time, never over a dialog or sheet, and never on a first screen that has not yet shown its content.

The arrow keys move the highlight, Enter picks the highlighted suggestion and searches, Escape closes the list and a second Escape clears the field. The field is a combobox and the list a listbox, so assistive technology reads the count and the highlighted suggestion. The typed part keeps its weight; the completion after it is set in semibold.

icon.$description: Action sheet action: icon in pressed state.

attachments.$description: Attachments: photos and files added to a note or a message. An 'Add photo or file' button opens the platform's own picker (the photo library, the camera, the files app); each item then shows as a tile, a thumbnail for a picture and an icon with the name and size for a file, with a progress bar while it uploads and a remove button. A file that fails says why under its tile. The tiles are a list, and each remove button names its item ('Remove site-plan.pdf').

tile-bg.$description: File tile ground, and the ground under a thumbnail while it loads.

name-type.$description: File name (one line, truncated in the middle by the app).

remove.$description: Remove button's drawn circle, over the tile's inline-end corner.

remove-icon.$description: The x in the remove button.

error-border.$description: Outline of a tile whose upload failed.

message-type.$description: Why an item failed, under its tile.

list-detail.$description: List-detail: a list and the item chosen from it, side by side where there is room and one after the other where there is not. From two-pane-min the list keeps list-width at the inline start and the detail fills the rest, the chosen row marked selected; narrower, the list is the screen and choosing a row moves forward to the detail, with Back to return. The chosen item survives the change of layout when a tablet turns or a window resizes.

list-width.$description: Width of the list pane beside the detail.

two-pane-min.$description: Width from which the list and the detail sit side by side on iOS and Android (the web switches above breakpoint.sm).

divider.$description: List detail: line between the panes.

selected.$description: Ground of the chosen row in the list pane.

empty.$description: 'Choose a note' in the detail pane before a row is chosen.

print-page.$description: Print page frame: margins, bleed, crop marks, running head and folio.

rule-gap.$description: Gap between the running head (and the folio) and its rule.

theme.fixed: registration marks print in black on every press

print-heading.$description: Print headings: space above and below each level, on the body baseline rhythm.

print-figure.$description: Print figure: image or chart with a caption below.

radius.$description: Image corner radius in print (half the screen radius).

print-footnote.$description: Footnotes: numbered notes set in micro type above the folio.

print-chart.$description: Print chart: the chart forms that print (dp-chart and dp-sparkline in desert-pants.typ), from the same chart spec as reference/charts.js. Mute everything and spend the focus once; every bar and dot is outlined in the chart ink, series lines are cased in it and carry a marker shape each, and values are labelled directly, so nothing depends on colour alone.

ink.$description: Outline of bars, columns, dots and markers; casing of series lines.

focus.$description: The one emphasis: the focus bar, point, line or series.

tick.$description: Title, tick labels, legend entries, annotations and values outside the focus.

axis.$description: Print chart: axis and zero baseline.

band.$description: Bar and column fill outside the focus; area fill; bands.

context.$description: Context lines and points (the series around the focus).

series-1.$description: Series 1 fill and line (grouped and stacked bars, categorical lines).

series-2.$description: Series 2 fill and line (grouped and stacked bars, categorical lines).

series-3.$description: Series 3 fill and line (grouped and stacked bars, categorical lines).

series-4.$description: Series 4 fill and line (grouped and stacked bars, categorical lines).

series-5.$description: Series 5 fill and line (grouped and stacked bars, categorical lines).

series-6.$description: Series 6 fill and line (grouped and stacked bars, categorical lines).

positive.$description: Diverging bars at or above zero.

line-width.$description: Print chart: series and focus lines.

casing-width.$description: Chart-ink casing on each side of a categorical series line.

outline-width.$description: Outline of bars, columns, dots and markers.

axis-width.$description: Print chart: axis and zero baseline.

dash.$description: Dash length of reference lines and waterfall connectors.

point-radius-focus.$description: Radius of the focus point at the end of a focus line (3pt).

bar-radius.$description: Corner radius at the value end of bars and columns.

bar-min.$description: Smallest drawn bar length, so a small non-zero value stays visible.

bar-gap-ratio.$description: Gap between neighbouring bars as a share of each bar's band (as on screen).

group-gap-ratio.$description: Gap between groups of bars as a share of the group's band (as on screen).

tick-count.$description: Target number of value ticks (steps of 1, 2 or 5 times a power of ten; as on screen).

tick-gap.$description: Gap between an axis and its tick labels (6pt).

label-gap.$description: Gap between a mark and its direct label (3pt).

title-gap.$description: Gap between the title and the plot (6pt).

legend-item-gap.$description: Gap between a legend swatch and its label (3pt).

legend-margin.$description: Space between the plot and the legend (6pt).

aspect.$description: Width to height of the plot when no height is given.

plot-max-height.$description: Largest plot height when no height is given (240pt).

spark-width.$description: Sparkline width when nothing else sets it (72pt).

spark-height.$description: Sparkline height: it sits in a line of body text (9pt).

print-poster.$description: Print poster: a scene (the infinite canvas) printed as one large sheet. The trim, a quiet border, a hairline frame, zone markers along the frame and a title block; the scene inside at one uniform scale K. Text is judged at the size it prints (declared world px x K x 0.75), against a floor per role.

inset.$description: Quiet border between the trim and the frame on every side (48pt): no ink lands in it.

zone-band.$description: Band between the frame and the inner rule that holds the zone markers (18pt).

zone-pitch.$description: Target size of a zone (4in): a sheet gets as many zone columns and rows as fit, at least two.

zone-type.$description: Zone markers (A B C along the top and bottom, 1 2 3 down the sides).

title-block-width.$description: Title block width (4in), in the bottom right corner of the design region.

title-block-title-type.$description: Sheet title in the title block.

title-block-meta-type.$description: Sheet id, revision, date and scale in the title block.

legend-swatch-width.$description: Length of a legend sample line in the title strip (36pt).

legend-swatch-height.$description: Height of a legend sample (6pt); the line sits on its centre.

legend-item-gap.$description: Gap between a legend sample and its name (6pt).

floor-title.$description: Smallest printed size of the scene title, in points: world px x K x 0.75 must reach it.

floor-section.$description: Smallest printed size of section headings, in points: world px x K x 0.75 must reach it.

floor-body.$description: Smallest printed size of body text: the reference role, in points: world px x K x 0.75 must reach it.

floor-caption.$description: Smallest printed size of captions and node text, in points: world px x K x 0.75 must reach it.

floor-label.$description: Smallest printed size of labels, node titles in small scenes and zone-scale annotations, in points: world px x K x 0.75 must reach it.

floor-micro.$description: Smallest printed size of units and suffixes, never sentences, in points: world px x K x 0.75 must reach it.

hairline-min.$description: Thinnest printed stroke, in points (strokes scale with K).

device-width.$description: Widest roll the sheet must fit (24in); a wider sheet whose height fits prints rotated.

flat-dpi.$description: Resolution of the flattened PNG proof (typst compile --format png --ppi).

flat-dpi-high.$description: Resolution of the full flattened derivative for printers that take only images.
